n: The story backs up to follow Aaron. After the brothers parted, he went to a Lamanite city they had named Jerusalem, after their ancestral homeland, near the borders of Mormon.

f.g: A New World city named after Lehi’s old home; it was later destroyed at Christ’s death.

n: Lamanites, Amalekites, and Amulonites built this great city together.

f.g: Nephite dissenters; some scholars think they are the Amlicites of Alma 2 under a variant spelling.

n: Though the Lamanites were hardened, the Nephite dissenters among them were harder still and led the Lamanites deeper into sin. Apostates often become the fiercest opponents.
Aaron begins preaching to the Amalekites in synagogues they built after the order of Nehor.

f.w: after the order of the Nehors

n: An Amalekite challenges him: have you seen an angel? Why don’t angels come to us? Aren’t we as good as your people?

f.w: Why do not angels appear unto us
f.g: Angels do appear — to those prepared by faith.

n: He continues: how do you know we need to repent? We’ve built sanctuaries and worship God, and we believe God will save everyone — Nehor’s doctrine exactly.

f.w: We do believe that God will save all men

n: Aaron goes straight to the core question: do you believe the Son of God will come to redeem mankind?

f.w: the Son of God shall come
f.g: Aaron focuses on Christ rather than arguing side issues.

n: The man rejects it: no one can know the future, and neither their fathers nor his own knew what they claimed.
Aaron opens the scriptures about Christ’s coming, the resurrection, and redemption only through Christ’s suffering, death, and atoning blood.
They grow angry, mock him, and refuse to listen.
Aaron leaves and goes to the village Ani-Anti, where he finds Muloki, Ammah, and others preaching and debating.

f.g: A Lamanite village near the city of Jerusalem.

n: Seeing hardened hearts, they move on to Middoni, where few believe.
Aaron and some companions are imprisoned; the rest escape.
Those in prison suffer greatly until Lamoni and Ammon free them, then they are fed and clothed.

f.w: delivered by the hand of Lamoni and Ammon

n: Released, they go right back to preaching — this was their first deliverance from prison.

f.g: Suggests they faced prison more than once.

n: Led by the Spirit, they preach in every Amalekite synagogue and Lamanite assembly that admits them.

f.w: whithersoever they were led by the Spirit

n: The Lord blesses them, and many come to the truth, recognizing their sins and their fathers’ false traditions.
Ammon and Lamoni return home to the land of Ishmael.
Lamoni no longer lets Ammon serve him — he now treats him as an honored teacher.
Lamoni builds synagogues and gathers his people to worship.
Lamoni teaches his people and announces they are free from his father’s oppressive rule, as his father had granted.
He also grants religious freedom: anyone in his realm may worship God as they choose.

f.w: the liberty of worshiping the Lord their God according to their desires

n: Ammon teaches Lamoni’s people daily and diligently, and they become zealous in keeping God’s commandments.
